decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar. Arcanine + Gengar lead provides immediate Intimidate to cushion Garchomp and Raichu physical pressure while allowing Gengar to safely Mega Evolve (using Protect turn 1 if Raichu is present to deny Nuzzle). Aerodactyl and Dragonite in the back offer Wide Guard protection against Heat Wave/Rock Slide, Tailwind speed control, and strong priority cleanup with Inner Focus ESpeed.
decisions.notebook: Goodra-Hisui: Modest, Leftovers (Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Body Press, Protect). Raichu: Timid, Lum Berry (Fake Out, Nuzzle, Thunderbolt, Protect). Primarina: Modest, Life Orb, Liquid Voice (Hydro Pump, Moonblast, Ice Beam, Protect). Garchomp: Jolly, Choice Scarf.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega is Charizard Y. Charizard + Raichu immediately pressures the likely Gengar/Aerodactyl mode: Fake Out denies Tailwind while Heat Wave breaks Aerodactyl’s Sash and damages Gengar. Garchomp supplies fast Rock Slide pressure after Aerodactyl is softened, while Primarina is the protected endgame cleaner into Dragonite, Krookodile, and Arcanine.

Charizard-Mega-Y sets Sun and threatens massive Heat Wave damage. Gengar Mega Protect guarantees safety on Turn 1 while establishing Shadow Tag to lock Charizard on the field. Switching Arcanine to Aerodactyl brings in Wide Guard and 4x effective Rock Slide pressure for Turn 2.

Mega Evolving establishes sun and makes Heat Wave the strongest available pressure into Gengar while still chipping Arcanine. Nuzzle is the key control: Raichu can act before unboosted Gengar and paralysis limits Mega Gengar’s speed and future Shadow Tag pressure. Fake Out cannot affect Ghost-type Gengar.

Raichu used Nuzzle turn 1 so Fake Out is unavailable. Both Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar outspeed Charizard-Y and Raichu (200 Spe vs max 167/178). Aerodactyl Rock Slide (83.8-158.8%) combined with Gengar Sludge Bomb (36.8-65.4%) guarantees a KO on Charizard-Y before it can attack if it does not Protect, removing the primary sun threat while Shadow Tag keeps both foes trapped.

Dragonite enters cleanly with excellent defensive matchups against Charizard's Sun-boosted Heat Wave (resisted) and Raichu. With Inner Focus and Life Orb, Dragonite offers immediate offensive threat with priority Extreme Speed to clear the 27% Raichu or a 4x super-effective Rock Slide into Charizard-Y, while Gengar (speed 200) outspeeds both trapped targets next turn.

Thunderbolt guarantees Aerodactyl’s removal from its shown HP, denying Tailwind and future Rock Slide. Charizard must Protect because Aerodactyl may be faster and Rock Slide is 4x effective; it also covers Gengar’s direct attack. Trading Raichu for Aerodactyl is favorable with Garchomp and Primarina preserved.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Aerodactyl + Mega Gengar mode uses Tailwind; Aerodactyl has Focus Sash, Wide Guard, and Taunt. Mega Gengar is vulnerable to Nuzzle and threatens Primarina with Sludge Bomb. Arcanine supplies Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and priority pressure. Preserve Primarina for cleanup rather than trading it into Gengar when possible.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega outspeeds Charizard-Mega-Y (200 vs max 167) and delivers 36.8-65.4% with Sludge Bomb, which combines with Dragonite's Rock Slide (94.6-178.4%) to guarantee a KO on Charizard before it can attack. Rock Slide's spread damage (31.1-65.2%) also finishes off Raichu (27% HP).

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Dragonite’s Rock Slide is the immediate game-losing threat to Charizard. Even with reduced odds, Protect is the only direct denial available. Nuzzle targets Dragonite to create a lasting paralysis chance for future turns; Gengar cannot be hit by Fake Out and Raichu’s low HP makes a switch unlikely to improve this turn’s Rock Slide matchup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl mode uses Tailwind; Aerodactyl has Focus Sash, Wide Guard, and Taunt. Mega Gengar is vulnerable to Nuzzle and threatens Primarina with Sludge Bomb. Arcanine supplies Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and priority pressure. Preserve Primarina for cleanup rather than trading it into Gengar when possible.

decisions.rationale: Both reserves must enter. Garchomp is the immediate answer to Dragonite with Choice Scarf Dragon Claw and can threaten Gengar with Stomping Tantrum; Primarina is unfortunately exposed to Gengar’s Sludge Bomb regardless of slot, so preserve Garchomp’s clean Dragonite matchup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl mode uses Tailwind; Aerodactyl has Focus Sash, Wide Guard, and Taunt. Mega Gengar is vulnerable to Nuzzle and threatens Primarina with Sludge Bomb. Arcanine supplies Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and priority pressure. Preserve Primarina for cleanup rather than trading it into Gengar when possible.

decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Mega Gengar and threatens an immediate Stomping Tantrum KO, while Primarina or Garchomp also threaten paralyzed Dragonite. Protecting Gengar while pivoting Dragonite to Arcanine safely applies Intimidate, blocks Garchomp's targeted move, locks Garchomp into a move under Choice Scarf, and positions Arcanine to resist Primarina's attacks in Sun.

Garchomp is Scarf-fast and Stomping Tantrum guarantees Mega Gengar’s KO if it does not Protect; Life Orb Ice Beam guarantees Dragonite’s KO. Trading Primarina to Sludge Bomb is preferable to Protecting it and allowing Dragonite’s 4x Ice Spinner to remove Garchomp, leaving no immediate answer to Gengar.

Garchomp is Scarf-locked into Stomping Tantrum at -1 Attack, dealing at most 68% to Gengar-Mega (100% HP) and 64% to Arcanine. Arcanine (115 Speed) naturally outspeeds Modest Primarina (max 112 Speed). Double-targeting Primarina with Gengar's Sludge Bomb (57-140%) and Arcanine's Sun-boosted Flare Blitz (28-54%) guarantees maximum pressure to KO Primarina before she can attack.

Scarf Garchomp is guaranteed ahead of Mega Gengar and threatens its Ground weakness. Hydro Pump is Primarina’s listed super-effective option into Arcanine and can remove it despite sun. This covers Gengar attacking by aiming to clear both foes; if Gengar uses its reduced-success Protect, Arcanine still falls and Primarina can survive for the endgame.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum, a Ground-type move. Switching Arcanine to Dragonite safely brings in a Flying-type immune to Ground, while Gengar Protects to block any attack targeted at its slot. With Dragonite on the field, Scarf Garchomp locked into Stomping Tantrum cannot deal any damage to Dragonite, securing an unlosable endgame.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp: Choice Scarf, locked into Stomping Tantrum.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is guaranteed faster than Mega Gengar and Stomping Tantrum cleanly removes its 16% HP before it can act. Taking the immediate KO avoids a Protect-assisted burn line and leaves only Arcanine plus the paralyzed Dragonite to handle.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum. Dragonite is immune to Ground moves as a Flying-type. Regardless of whether Garchomp attacks Gengar or Dragonite, Stomping Tantrum cannot touch Dragonite, and Dragonite's 4x super-effective 100% accurate Life Orb Ice Spinner guarantees a 100%+ OHKO on Garchomp (102.8-181.4%) to secure the series win.

Garchomp is Choice-locked, and Stomping Tantrum is the only available damaging action that can remove the 16% Gengar. Dragonite is immune, so targeting it wastes the turn and leaves Gengar alive. Consecutive Protect has reduced odds; take the guaranteed-pressure line.

reflections.summary: Early offense from Mega Gengar and Dragonite eliminated Charizard-Y and Raichu simultaneously, while an Arcanine Intimidate pivot allowed Dragonite to comfortably clean up Choice Scarf Garchomp with Ice Spinner.
reflections.adjustment: Against teams with Scarf ground attackers like Garchomp, switch out Mega Gengar earlier rather than sacrificing it to locked Stomping Tantrums to keep endgame board presence completely healthy.
reflections.notebook: Opponent sets confirmed: Garchomp (Choice Scarf, Jolly, Stomping Tantrum/Rock Slide/Dragon Claw/Poison Jab), Primarina (Life Orb, Modest, Liquid Voice), Raichu (Lum Berry, Timid, Lightning Rod), Charizard-Y (Charizardite Y, Timid). Intimidate Arcanine + Ice Spinner Dragonite reliably handles Scarf Garchomp endgames.

reflections.summary: Lost because the Charizard-Y/Raichu lead was exposed to Dragonite’s Rock Slide, costing both immediately; Mega Charizard Y was a poor centerpiece into revealed Rock coverage and Mega Gengar pressure. The forced four offered no alternate bench selection, but the Mega/lead plan did not suit this mode.
reflections.adjustment: Next game lead Garchomp + Raichu and keep Charizard/Primarina back; use Raichu disruption and Garchomp pressure before exposing Charizard to Dragonite/Aerodactyl Rock Slide. Do not lock Garchomp into Stomping Tantrum while Mega Gengar can repeatedly Protect.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl mode uses Tailwind; Aerodactyl has Focus Sash, Wide Guard, and Taunt. Mega Gengar threatens Primarina with Sludge Bomb and can use Protect repeatedly to punish Choice locks. Arcanine supplies Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and priority pressure. Dragonite is Life Orb Adamant with Inner Focus, ExtremeSpeed, Rock Slide, and Ice Spinner; respect its Rock Slide against Charizard. Against this opponent, avoid centering the early game on Mega Charizard Y and preserve Primarina for cleanup rather than trading it into Gengar when possible.
